answer: Distinct Summit Routing requires each new identity to arrive by a route no existing identity has used: its first three interactions must land on disjoint partners, and those partners must themselves sit in different saffron-labeled neighborhoods. Routes are logged, so clones cluster and get filtered. An attacker pays for three genuinely separate partner subgraphs per identity, roughly tripling coordination cost, while honest agents share a dense shale of overlapping paths and pass cheaply.
